title: Establish graceful slot-based degradation and canary probe plan for short-lived interactive conversations
creator: Asha Patel
description: PRD-level ticket to define SLO bands, error budget behavior, and a detailed canary probe plan for short-lived interactive conversations (typical session length 1-20 turns). Scope covers hosted and dedicated modes for streaming-first endpoints and introduces a slot-based degradation model that degrades QoS in discrete steps (slots) rather than binary fallback. This ticket clarifies acceptance criteria, synthetic probe design, rollout gates, monitoring dashboards, and required infra/observability work. Excludes implementation tasks (ENG tickets referenced in dependencies).
acceptance_criteria: SLO definitions included for Hosted API and Dedicated (reserved) for first-token and per-token tail latency, availability, and 5xx error rate.
Error budget math and burn-rate behavior documented for phased canaries with explicit thresholds for abort/rollback and automatic pause conditions.
A synthetic canary probe harness specified (traffic profile, session lengths, random seed, health signal extraction) and a Grafana dashboard mockup linked.
Slot-based degradation model defined with at least 3 discrete slots (Normal, Degraded-A, Degraded-B) and mapping to user-visible behaviors and billing/route policies.
Rollout gating policy documented: required green for synthetic probes, green for a 1% real-traffic shadow window, then step ramps with retrospective analysis windows defined.
Ownership and playbook for failure modes (auto-rollback, shunt-to-fallback, customer notification) assigned and acknowledged by SRE/Support.
PRD reviewed and approved by Product, SRE, and Design with comments addressed.
Links to required implementation tickets and observability tasks added to dependencies and attachments.
steps: Baseline collection: run historical analysis on three representative customer cohorts to establish baseline p50/p95/p99 and per-token tail for streaming endpoints.
Define SLO bands: Normal/Degraded-A/Degraded-B with explicit numeric thresholds for hosted vs dedicated.
Design synthetic canary harness: session generator, seeded prompts, target model variants (float32 vs quantized fallback), and evaluation script for fidelity regressions.
Specify ramp plan: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with time windows and rollback criteria tied to error budget burn rate and p99 delta limits.
Create dashboards and alerts: Grafana panels for probe health, burn-rate, tail latency by slot, and tenant impact score.
Coordinate SRE runbook and PagerDuty escalation path for early canary phases.
Final PRD signoff and handoff to engineering for execution tickets.
metrics: p99 first-token latency (streaming-first): target hosted < 450ms, dedicated < 300ms under steady-state
per-token 95/99 tail latency: target per-token p99 < 60ms for hosted, < 35ms for dedicated under typical batch sizes
error budget consumption: percent of error budget burned per hour and 24h burn-rate
customer-impact score: weighted score combining error-rate, p99 delta, and % traffic affected by slot changes
rollout_gates: Gate 0 (synthetic probe green): synthetic probe p99 delta < 1.5x baseline AND error budget consumption < 3% in 1h window
Gate 1 (shadow real traffic): 1% mirrored real traffic for 2h with customer-impact score < 1.0 and no user-facing errors observed
Gate 2 (canary ramp): step ramps with acceptance window 6h each. Abort if 24h burn-rate > 3x or p99 delta > 2x baseline for any representative cohort
Gate 3 (full rollout): 24h observation with automated throttling in place; must maintain error budget consumption < 10% and availability targets
Auto-pause conditions: sustained per-tenant burn-rate beyond configured hysteresis OR any high-severity customer complaint correlated to canary sessions
notes_and_tradeoffs: Slot-based degradation reduces noisy black-box fallbacks by exposing graduated QoS which is easier for clients to detect and handle, at the cost of increased routing and billing complexity.
We accept slightly higher p95 for Hosted in Degraded-A to preserve overall throughput; Dedicated tenants remain prioritized where feasible.
Synthetic probes may not catch semantic regression; include a small human-reviewed prompt set in the probe for quality sanity checks (weekly).
Risk: automated ramping increases chance of cross-tenant blast radius; mitigations include per-tenant rate limits and circuit-breakers referenced in dependencies.
Decision deferred: exact billing behavior during degraded slots (discount vs full) — requires finance and legal input (follow-up action created).
